utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-96-23/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I see that the Prosecution is present. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. Mr. Jovanovic for the Defence. Mr. Zelenovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, have you had an opportunity to briefly discuss with counsel the new document that has meanwhile been filed with the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I had the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I worked on the basis of a courtesy copy that was provided to the Chamber when I was not in the premises of this Tribunal. I take it that this document has been filed on the 16th of January. These are the transcript pages 6560 up to and including the cover page 6580. Thank you. Then I have a few questions in relation to the latest filing, mainly to ensure that there's no ambiguity whatsoever. I draw the attention to paragraph 5.4 in relation to 5.9. Is it well understood that because of the role Mr. Zelenovic played, that he intends to plead guilty on rape and torture even where he did not personally commit it -- personally rape the victims, but his role in its entirety makes him a co-perpetrator? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you can see, the distinction in relation to incident paragraph 5.4, he is actually here pleading to have aided and abetted in relation to the victim 75 that he did not rape on that occasion. And he was actually at that time also not in charge, but Gojko Jankovic was. Therefore, we have here aiding and abetting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to apologise, because my question should have been different. What I should have asked you is whether 5.4 should be understood as a substantial assistance by the accused in the rape of victim FWS-75 amounting to aiding and abetting. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's the understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, that's the understanding of the Defence as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We see this as aiding and abetting. It's not as substantial as to amount to co-perpetration. I think that all instances where it amounts to co-perpetration, it is explicitly stated so. And in this particular case, this is aiding and abetting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, for example, would be true for paragraph 6.14 in relation to 6.6. I'm here thinking about the two identified and two unidentified women where Mr. Zelenovic is co-perpetrator in relation to all four women. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, that's your position as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then finally I turn to paragraph 9.13 -- 9.3, I'm sorry. The rape under count 49 -- in 9.2 we see an incident where Mr. Zelenovic personally raped victim FWS-87 and the other co-perpetrators raped the other women, the other -- yes, that is FWS-75 and two other women. In 9.3, it reads, "by the foregoing acts and omissions, Dragan Zelenovic committed, rape ..." Is that co-perpetration for all rapes or is it limited to victim FWS-87?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is co-perpetration in relation to all the victims. As it is also expressed in 9.2, co-perpetrators is particularly mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, that's your position as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my interpretation is that in this particular case this involves the rape of victim 75 by Mr. Zelenovic. It was qualified as rape. My understanding is that he did not participate in the rape of victim 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me read 9.2. "There, Dragan Zelenovic raped FWS-87 while the other co-perpetrators raped the other women." It is a puzzle for me what you just said. You said, "my interpretation is that in this particular case this involves the rape of victim 75 by Mr. Zelenovic." It was qualified as rape. My understanding is that he did not participate in the rape of victim 87. That's a puzzle to me in view of the text of the submission of yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Dragan Zelenovic, according to the text of the indictment, 9.2, raped victim 87. My interpretation is that co-perpetrators, that is to say, other persons raped other women on that occasion. So co-perpetration pertains to other individuals who, on that occasion, raped other women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does he plead guilty to, or does he intend to plead guilty to co-perpetratorship, that is, shared responsibility for all the rapes or just for the rape he committed in respect of victim FWS-87.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My interpretation is that he pleads guilty to raping victim 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, it seems that, first of all, I do not understand under those circumstances the use of the word "co-perpetratorship," because if I understand you well, it's just Mr. Zelenovic raping one woman, another one raping another woman, which does not result in co-perpetratorship; whereas if you have other people rape women, then you could consider, and then you'd use the word co-perpetratorship, that as a shared responsibility for all the rapes, just as Mr. Zelenovic seems to accept a responsibility on the other occasion - I think I'm talking about 6.10 - where -- no, 6.6 it is, where he did not rape, himself, any of the women, but nevertheless considers himself an aider and abettor -- no, co-perpetrator in 6.6, I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one correction. In 6.6, we have the similar situation that Mr. Zelenovic himself raped one woman and the others were raped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And also perhaps for Mr. Jovanovic's benefit, if we look at the factual basis of the plea agreement, paragraph 22, actually, Mr. Zelenovic mentioned that he and his co-perpetrators took out the four women, and that he himself raped 87 while the co-perpetrators raped the other three women. So I think it's probably an error by Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, so the issue is here whether Mr. Zelenovic, if he would plead guilty to this paragraph 9.3, whether he exclusively sees his role as in relation to victim FWS-87 or whether, in those circumstances, he accepts, as he does in 6.6, that although he raped only one woman, that those present raping several women were co-perpetrators and therefore share responsibility, which of course would -- is what one would understand by the term "co-perpetratorship." Because otherwise these are several separated offences. It might not make that much of a difference on the whole of the case, as a matter of fact, but I leave it up to you to present your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see the difference in relation to the description of events in paragraph 6.6, because in 6.6 and similarly in the factual basis or statement of facts, it is stated that Dragan Zelenovic was the one who decided which woman will be allocated to which man, so to speak. And on that basis, he accepts his role as a co-perpetrator, because that was his role in relation to other victims. He was the one who decided which woman would be assigned, so to speak, to which man. We don't have that type of a situation in paragraph 9.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, that's all fine. It's not the Bench who enters into a plea agreement; it is the parties who do so. And now for the second time, after yesterday, a lot of confusion, a lot of misunderstanding, a lot of -- well, a lot of doubts as to what actually was the subject of the agreement ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will give you -- yes, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: What you said wasn't translated, so will you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise. I will repeat it. Mr. Zelenovic will plead guilty in accordance with the text of the amended and redacted indictment and as is stated in the statement of facts. Wherever it is stated that he acted as a co-perpetrator, he pleads guilty to co-perpetratorship, just to avoid any further ambiguities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, you have heard what Mr. Jovanovic just said. You have the text in front of you. I take it that you understand the difference between co-perpetratorship and committing a rape where others commit a rape as well. That means that you accept that in this context you share with your co-perpetrators responsibility, criminal responsibility, for the rapes committed in that context, even though you yourself raped only victim FWS-87. You understand the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic just told us that you'll enter a plea on the basis of your understanding of count 49, that is, in relation to 9.2 in the indictment, that the understanding of entering a plea - and of course we then would expect that it would be a guilty plea - would be on the basis of accepting a shared responsibility for the whole of the events that is in relation to all women raped. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you accept that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think everything has been clarified in relation to what actually the plea will be about. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, I suggest that we do it the following way: I take it that if Mr. Zelenovic pleads guilty to the counts specified in the new document, which is not an amended indictment but just a document which gives us further insight on what exactly is understood when Mr. Zelenovic enters a plea, that once he has entered a plea, that you'll withdraw all the remaining counts or remaining parts of the counts, and you would need leave of the Chamber to withdraw these counts. I suggest to you that you apply for that leave now, that we'll grant leave, and that after Mr. Zelenovic has entered his pleas on certain counts, that you'll then withdraw the remainder of the counts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that requires that you now ask our leave to withdraw the remaining counts after Mr. Zelenovic has entered his pleas, and in accordance with the document as you have filed it, together with Mr. Jovanovic, yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can do that. And I have to make -- draw your attention to one minor issue that relates to the plea agreement. It's the plea agreement, paragraph 3(A). It relates to the withdrawal of charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what the intention was of the parties is to withdraw all accumulated charges related to the events so that he is pleading guilty to seven counts of crime against humanity and that we intended to withdraw the war crime charges, the violations of the laws and customs of war. In this context, there is a minor inaccuracy in paragraph 3(A), and we found it out yesterday when Mr. Jovanovic and I were actually redacting the indictment. We have listed here in this paragraph six counts to be withdrawn. It's actually seven counts. What is omitted in the plea agreement is count 8. So today the Prosecution would request leave to be allowed to withdraw the seven counts of violations of the laws and customs of war, these counts being count 7, count 8, count 15, count 16, count 43, count 44, and count 50. That's the -- that's what we would request the Trial Chamber to allow us to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see that already reflected. Let me just check that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It is reflected, actually, in the document, and that's how we saw that it was missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Thank you for this clarification. I suggest that the Chamber now considers whether leave should be granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted, which of course, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, doesn't mean that it's yet withdrawn. But I take it that once we have come to the selective invitation to enter a plea, that once we are at a point where all the guilty pleas you expect are there, that you then withdraw the remainder of the counts, which leaves us without any need to further invite Mr. Zelenovic to enter pleas. Then, Mr. Zelenovic, I'll go -- first of all, you followed all the discussions. They were quite some detailed discussions. The Chamber understood both from the plea agreement and from the submission of yesterday that it's your wish to change your plea in respect of many of the counts of the indictment. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We also understood that this wish is the result of a -- is part of a plea agreement in which you voluntarily entered -- assisted in the, most likely, in the legal negotiations with Mr. Jovanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'll invite you to enter your new plea on the counts of the indictment as I'll put to you, and I'll go through the indictment in some more detail, as I usually do, in order to make sure that you fully understand what you're pleading to. In the indictment we find in paragraphs 1 -- in paragraph 1, that's 1.1 to 1.4, we find a general background description. Then we find in paragraph 2, under 2.4, we find some further details about you, Mr. Zelenovic. This information includes that you were a member of the Dragan Nikolic unit and that you were a soldier and a de facto military policeman. Then under 4 we find some general allegations in which it is explained - and I'm referring now to 4.5 - that witnesses and victims are identified in this indictment using codenames or pseudonyms, and one example now remains as given of such a pseudonym which is the example of victim FWS-75. It only explains the technique used in identifying persons, victims especially, in the indictment. Then the charges against you more specifically, Mr. Zelenovic, are in relation to torture and rape committed in Buk Bijela, set out in paragraphs 5.1 up to and including 5.5 of the indictment. 5.4 of the indictment describes an event where witness FWS-75 was interrogated, was interrogated among others by you. She was warned not to lie or otherwise she would be raped by soldiers and killed afterwards. But since victim FWS-75 did not answer the question sufficiently, she was taken out to another room, and there at least 10 unidentified soldiers have raped her. You did not personally rape the victim on that occasion. The other incident described under paragraph 5 is that another witness, FWS-87, a 15-year-old girl, was interrogated by you and three unidentified soldiers in a room at Buk Bijela, and that during the interrogation she was accused of -- the victim was accused of not telling the truth; that then the interrogators removed her clothing and each one raped her. And it further gives details about the rape and the threats and violence used. This, Mr. Zelenovic, is legally qualified as -- as far as 5.4 is concerned, aiding and abetting, to torture and rape; and as far as 5.5 is concerned, committing torture and rape. So the aiding and abetting is in relation to victim FWS-75, and the commission of torture and rape in relation to victim FWS-87 - that's the incident in paragraph 5.5 - is -- that's the rape and the torture. Count 5 thus understood reads that you aided and abetted and/or committed torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Zelenovic, how do you plead to count 5, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record the guilty plea on count 5.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 6, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal, as explained to you before. How do you plead to count 6, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record the guilty plea on count 6.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on Mr. Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can barely hear the accused, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, you are invited to speak a bit louder. That's also because you are at a distance from the microphone now. If you enter any further new pleas. We now move, Mr. Zelenovic, to torture and rape committed at the Foca High School. After a brief description of circumstances at the Foca High School about detention and about physical/psychological circumstances, the indictment becomes more detailed and describes incidents, and I start with 6.6; that on the 6th or 7th of July, 1992, you, in concert with other co-perpetrators, have selected four women, two of them unidentified - one, FWS-75 and one being FWS-87 - you have selected them out of a group of detainees; that you led these women to another classroom where unidentified soldiers stood waiting; and that you then decided which woman should go to which man. The women were ordered to remove their clothes, and at that occasion, you, Mr. Zelenovic, you raped victim FWS-75 and the other perpetrators -- co-perpetrators, as a matter of fact, raped the other women. So that's one incident including four women, you being charged with co-perpetration in respect of all women. Then 6.7, the incident described in 6.7 is not part of the new plea, and I therefore move to 6.8, which is one incident described between -- or about 8th of July and about 13th of July, where victims FWS-75 and FWS-87 were taken from the Foca High School to an apartment building called Brena. You are charged there, Mr. Zelenovic, with having raped on that occasion both victim FWS-75 and victim FWS-87. Then there are two other occasions described under 6.9 of the indictment, two other occasions or incidents where you and several other but unidentified soldiers took victims FWS-75 and FWS-87 to Brena and that you raped them. 6.9 reads that "On these occasions, the accused raped FWS-75 and FWS-87." So two occasions in which you committed rape against both women. Then there's another incident described under 6.10 where victims FWS-75 and FWS-87 were taken by you to an abandoned house of a Muslim policeman in Gornje Polje where you raped victim FWS-87. By these acts I just specified to you, you are charged, Mr. Zelenovic, that you committed rape and torture in relation to two unidentified women and victim FWS-75 and FWS-87. Count 13 deals with the torture charge. I'll read it to you. "Torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal." Mr. Zelenovic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record a guilty plea on count 13.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 14, Mr. Zelenovic, reads: "Rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal." How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record a guilty plea on count 14.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now move, Mr. Zelenovic, to events that happened at the Partizan Sports Hall. We find them in paragraphs -- in paragraph 7 of the indictment, where first a general description of the context, of the circumstances, are given. Specifically, one incident you are charged with we find in paragraph 7.13, which reads that "In July 1992, witness FWS-87 was frequently taken out and raped, and that on one occasion, witness FWS-87 was gang-raped by four men, including Dragan Zelenovic." And this happened in July 1992. This results in charges against you under count 41, torture, and 42, rape. And the charges are limited to victim FWS-87 only. This clarifies what is found at 7.26 of the indictment. Count 41, Mr. Zelenovic, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal. In relation to this one incident at Partizan Sports Hall, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record a guilty plea on count 41.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 42, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Again, Mr. Zelenovic, in relation to the event just described, how do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record the guilty plea on count 42.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move to the last count brought against you, Mr. Zelenovic. The specific event is described in 9.2 of the indictment, which I'll read to you: "On or about the 30th of October, 1992, the three above-mentioned perpetrators, that is Dragan Zelenovic, Gojko Jankovic and Janko Janjic, took FWS-75, FWS-87 and two other women into an apartment near the fish restaurant in Foca." There, Dragan Zelenovic, you raped FWS-87, while the other co-perpetrators raped the other women. By these acts, Mr. Zelenovic, by these acts and omissions, you are charged with having committed rape, co-perpetration of rape, in respect of all these women, although you personally raped only - that means the act of rape was committed by you only - in respect of witness FWS-87. In respect of all these four women, and understanding the charges to be co-perpetrators, on count 49, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal, how do you plead, Mr. Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please record the guilty plea on count 49.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, the Chamber will have to satisfy itself that the guilty pleas you have now entered have been made voluntarily, that no threat or coercion was exercised, that you're informed, that your guilty pleas are not equivocal, and that there is a sufficient factual basis for the crime and for your participation in it. We have spent a lot of time on a proper understanding of what you actually pleaded guilty to, and the Chamber, until now, has no reason to assume that your plea was not made voluntarily or that any threats or coercion was exercised, that your plea was entered uninformed, that your plea was not unequivocal, that there was no sufficient factual basis for the crime and for your participation. If there's anything one of the parties would like to submit in relation to these requirements, they are invited to do so at this moment. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise for the Defence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Defence includes counsel and accused. Mr. Zelenovic, may I take it that you share the view of Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, the newly entered pleas are accepted by the Trial Chamber. This means that the Chamber makes a corresponding finding of guilt on each of these counts, and again the findings of guilt should be understood together with the document filed yesterday, where the details were set out, and should also be understood in light of the clarifications that have been given during today's hearing. Mr. Zelenovic, this Chamber finds you guilty under count 5 of the indictment, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal. This Chamber finds you guilty on count 6, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. The Chamber, Mr. Zelenovic, finds you guilty under count 13, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal. And the Chamber finds you guilty under count 14, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. The Chamber further finds you guilty, Mr. Zelenovic, under count 41, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal, and count 42, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Finally, Mr. Zelenovic, this Chamber finds you guilty under count 49 of the indictment, rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, may I take it that this is the moment where you will use the leave granted to you to withdraw the remaining counts of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With the leave of the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution withdraws the remaining counts, them being count 7, count 8, count 15, count 16, count 43, count 44, and count 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it also those parts of the counts that were not covered by the newly entered guilty pleas, the Chamber would, in order to avoid whatever confusion, would like you to file a precise specification of all the counts withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then there's no need at this moment to deal with any of the other counts, them being withdrawn and no new pleas entered there. Next issue is the scheduling of a sentencing hearing. Could I hear from the parties how much time -- Mr. Zelenovic, you may be seated. We're dealing now with practical and technical matters. Can I get an indication from the parties how much time they need for the preparation of a sentencing hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not need much time because the Prosecution does not intend to call witnesses in that hearing. So we actually need only, I would say, two weeks to file the sentencing briefs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two weeks for filing the sentencing brief. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But I assume that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course I will ask Mr. Jovanovic how much time he would use and what he intends to present in support of the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would ask for a longer period of time, perhaps around 30 days. The reason being that when presenting our case, when presenting our position pertaining to our proposal for the sentence, I would like to provide some details about the health condition of the accused, which is not great. He is under observation of doctors at the Detention Unit. We are expecting to receive his medical history. And let me just inform you that Mr. Zelenovic recently was hospitalised; therefore, his health condition is rather poor. In addition to supporting our sentence proposal with our arguments, we would also like to enclose the opinion of a medical expert as well as an opinion of a psychologist who would speak of traumas that victims suffered. Given that Mr. Zelenovic pleaded guilty to these crimes, it will not be necessary for the victims to come again to testify here and to be traumatised again. This is something that we want to support with the finding of our expert psychologist, and we need more time for that than the two weeks that the Prosecution asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we believe that four weeks would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties are granted four weeks to file their pre-sentencing briefs. Of course it makes no sense at this moment to have a date already set, but the registrar is instructed to consult with the Chamber in the near future for setting a date for a sentencing hearing. Mr. Jovanovic, do you intend to -- you said that you did not want to call victims as witnesses. Do you have in mind at all to call any witnesses for the purposes of sentencing?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, except for the experts, should the Chamber find this necessary, the psychologist whose expert report would be enclosed with our brief. We can call the expert, if necessary, for him or her to answer questions by the Bench or the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the expert report would be submitted to the Chamber, then, of course, the Prosecution could, I would say, in analogy with Rule 94 bis, could express whether it accepts the report, whether it wants the expert to be called for -- to be cross-examined. Of course the Chamber, even if the Prosecution would not wish to call the expert, the Chamber might have the wish to call the expert. So let's first wait and see what the expert report tells us, and then we can decide whether there's any need to have the expert to be called. Thank you for that. So the four weeks -- today we are the 17th of January. Four weeks from now would be -- Madam Registrar, the exact date, four weeks would be? I haven't got my agenda with me here. That would be the 15th of February?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 14th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So sentencing briefs to be filed not later than the 14th of February. Are there any other motions? Are there any matters to be raised at this moment, apart from - and I'll pay some attention to that - the health of Mr. Zelenovic? We'll ask him before we adjourn whether the Chamber should be informed about details of what happened to him. Yes, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is one matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I'll refer to our confidential filing, the confidential joint motion for a consideration of guilty plea, which was filed on the 14th of December, 2006. We have actually mentioned already in that motion that during this hearing, the parties would request that a Trial Chamber's order, that the documents filed in that motion be made public --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- because we filed it confidentially, but there is no need now any longer for this confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jovanovic, any objection against this?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber, having in mind the requirement of transparency as already expressed in Rule 62 ter, under (C), grants your request, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff. Therefore, the confidentiality of filed documents as mentioned by you now are public documents. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing else, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, before we adjourn, it was mentioned that you recently were hospitalised and that your health situation was not very good. Apart from what role that may play in sentencing, if you'd like to inform the Chamber whether or not, in private session, about it, if you consider it good for the Chamber to know what health problems you are facing at this moment, please inform us. At the same time, I say that there's no duty, no obligation, to inform us. It's up to you whether you consider it wise to inform us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am being treated now at the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand your answer to be that your medical problems are taken care of and that further details about your health problems are not such that the Chamber should know about it. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My Defence counsel will inform you. My Defence counsel talked to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, do you see any reason at this moment to inform the Chamber? If you'd prefer to do so in private session, please ask to go into private session. If you say no, it's not relevant, then we'll leave it up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in my brief, sentencing brief, I will inform you of the medical history and everything else that is necessary. As for the treatment that Mr. Zelenovic is receiving, I think that everything is in order. I'm in contact with the relevant authorities in the Detention Unit. Mr. Zelenovic is receiving the necessary treatment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this information. We will adjourn sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 10.21 a.m. sine die
